data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB, NHATS), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, data.nasa.gov), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.name: Radio Science (RS)
record.description: The Radio Science (RS) experiment on MESSENGER is designed to make use of the existing radio communications equipment on the spacecraft to study Mercury's gravitational field, libration, and global shape. The communications system consists of redundant X-band transponders, two phased arrays, a medium-gain and a low-gain antenna. The phased arrays are electronically steerable passive waveguide antennas fed by solid state power amplifiers. Tracking of the spacecraft to 0.1 mm/s rms error over a 60 second integration period is required for accurate determination of spacecraft velocity and position. Velocity is used to determine the gravitational effects on the spacecraft which in turn will be used in determination of Mercury's internal mass distribution. Accurate position of the spacecraft is required by the Laser Altimeter and also to determine the libration of Mercury. Radio occultations will be used to determine the shape of the planet and the amplitude of the libration.
